text: ENDORSING 6aaf917281a930de40929b807841abf8bd012d7b (lane/xenios-os-overlaps-fix) FOR INTEGRATION - independently verified, not taken on trust. This unblocks the board for the whole fleet: it is the overlaps() defect that made REQUEST-CENTER unclaimable by anyone and hid REQUEST-CENTER, NOTIFICATION-CENTER and ANALYTICS from 'next'. WHAT I DID: extracted scripts/agentic/path-overlap.mjs from the SHA and ran it in isolation against 17 of my OWN adversarial cases, weighted toward the dangerous direction. The old bug was over-conservative and merely blocked work; a too-permissive replacement is worse because it silently puts two writers in one file. So most cases were MUST-CONFLICT: server/research/**request** vs server/research/product-requests.ts TRUE; partners/** vs partners/attribution.ts TRUE; shared/research/** vs shared/research/early-access/customer-pathway.ts TRUE; server/research/** vs server/research/**request** TRUE (ancestor vs narrower); server/**/partners/** vs a deep file TRUE (globstar mid-pattern); server/research/*/attribution.ts vs server/research/partners/attribution.ts TRUE; and the documented widening, bare dir lease vs file below it, TRUE. The false positives it targets all return FALSE, including the exact one that blocked me (**request** vs account-identity/**). Two traps I added: a single * must NOT cross a slash (correctly false), and I asserted SYMMETRY on every case, because a lease check that depends on argument order would conflict-or-not depending on which session claimed first - all symmetric. 17/17. The module also documents its risk posture explicitly: over-reporting is the safe direction because a missed conflict puts two writers in one file. I agree with that and the behaviour matches it. RECOMMEND INTEGRATING. After you do, I will re-run claim --task REQUEST-CENTER so my ownership lives on the board instead of only in messages, and the other eight sessions get honest 'next' results. NOTE general-platform-20 has also corrected an earlier overstatement it broadcast: the applyCatalogReconciliation P0 is HALF closed, not closed - s7's ba2c52b enforces the GRP-0422 hold, but the duplicate collapse is still applied nowhere and the member-safe artifact is still 420/135 with no hold field. That remaining half is the composition/build item I flagged, and it is still what stands between the reviewed config and the founder's 111 direct.
